# Fifteen puzzle: Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `fifteen-puzzle.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.42) and `fifteen-puzzle-rules.soar` (11 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`; `tools/rosie_grid.py`). Generated 18 Nov 2026. Needs Soar 9.6.6 (or the PyPI soar-sml bindings).

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . fifteen-puzzle.soar --seed 1 --cap 60000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . fifteen-puzzle.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_moves.py fifteen-puzzle init-i15puzzle.world

`python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with another example state as the initial world.

## Results (library v2.42, 18 Nov 2026)

Example states (`gen.py WORLD`, `run_agent.py --check`): init-i15puzzle: goal false, failure false; final-i15puzzle: goal true, failure false.

Seeds 1-3, cap 60,000 decisions; plans replayed independently by `check_moves.py` (legality from the action statements, the losing conditions, the goal).

| Seed | Outcome | Decisions | Actions | Replay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | success | 12 | 1 | goal holds |
| 2 | success | 16 | 1 | goal holds |
| 3 | success | 12 | 1 | goal holds |

## Translation

- Operator slide-block (argument1 = the block, argument2 = the clear location), statement 5; adjacent (statement 7) is a
  static relation between locations, a block being adjacent to what its location is adjacent to (A-G1); clear is a
  maintained one-argument relation (statement 6).
- The goal is expanded over the blocks of the world file: every block is on the location with its value (A-G3).
Propose initialize-fifteen-puzzle when its conditions below hold.

The assumption codes (A-S, A-G, A-C, A-P) are explained in `tools/rosie_grid.py` and `../../PILOT.md`.
